address: 's-Gravesandestraat 55 (Hotel Arena), Amsterdam-Oost: 1890 former orphanage (Roman Catholic Burgerweeshuis) with 2000s hotel wings, red brick with a glazed pavilion
notes: Hotel Arena, 's-Gravesandestraat 55 / Sint Jansstraat (BAG pand 0363100012236788: built 1890; 38 dwellings, a hotel, an assembly and an office unit; 4,757 m2): the former Roman Catholic orphanage on the Oosterpark, converted to the Hotel Arena in 2000 and extended on the south side in the 2010s. Three walls are photographed: the old north wings (w04-341, panorama 2020-04-24: red brick, ground floor of segmental-arched cross windows in white frames, upper floor of tall white-surrounded windows, pale stone string courses), the new hotel wing (w03-162, 2021-05-12: buff horizontally-ribbed brick, deep-reveal dark window openings, a glazed curtain-wall attic, the Hotel Arena entrance gate wall in front) and the glazed garden pavilion on the south (w01-161, 2022-03-23: a glass ground floor under a thin projecting roof with a glass box above and the old slate roof with a timber gable behind).

Modelled: the old north wings (panels 210, 232, 56, all 3 storeys, red brick, cross windows with white frames, stone string courses; segmental-arched ground windows under a brick arch band with stone imposts (layered kit); the photographed relieving arches have a brick tympanum over a flat-headed window and a stone keystone, drawn as glazed segmental heads) as one group; the new wing (panels 2 and 373: 4 storeys, buff brick, plain deep-reveal windows) and the garden pavilion (panels 0 and 314) as a curtain-wall group. Roofs and every unlisted wall are the 3DBAG LoD2.2 shell in the old-brick colour.

Simplified: the new wing's glass attic is the same window grid as the floors below (the kit has no per-storey system switch), the ribbed buff brick is plain wall colour, the pavilion's thin roof plate and the timber gable are 3DBAG roof geometry only. Not drawn: the entrance gate wall with HOTEL ARENA lettering (a free-standing wall outside the pand), the cast-iron fence on the north side, the round chapel apse (curved wall facets keep the 3DBAG shell).

Measured 2026-10-14 (measure.ts, evidence in measured.json): groups 0, 1, 2 take the photo's wall and glass colour, window shape, bay count and front class; walls[0] glass #52463d not used (not darker than the wall #70574d by 10 L*, or tinted): kit glass kept; walls[1] wall split #af875c | #56443d at 70 % (dE 40.1); walls[2] glass #2d221d not used (not darker than the wall #3c352f by 10 L*, or tinted): kit glass kept.

Refit 2026-10-25 (issue #59): walls[0] (w07-340L) is two tall storeys under a frieze, not three: segmental-arched ground windows sill 0.41 h 0.44, first-floor cross windows sill 0.18 h 0.51 (storeyShapes), 1.7 m wide (likeness WARN, was FAIL). walls[1] (w03-162L) is five hotel floors on the 17.9 m wing: three of sunlit ribbed buff brick #d4955e with punched windows and a two-storey glass curtain attic (glazedStoreys 3, 4); the dark split was the HOTEL ARENA gate wall in front, removed. walls[2] was the curtain-wall pavilion, but its main panel 0 (w06-161) is the old north-south wing seen past the garden arcade: now the old-wing brick bay grid like walls[0]; the glazed garden pavilion (w01-161, 2022) is its one-storey glass ground on panels 239/300 (walls[4], 5.8 m) with the set-back glass box on panel 314 (walls[3], curtain wall; no crop matches the set-back panel). Gate misreads, allowed as inferred: walls[1] photo wall #382e27 is the shadowed gate wall over the lower two storeys (the wing above is sunlit buff, #de9a5e on the four-storey read); walls[2] model elevation at panel 0 is walls[1]`s wing standing in front of it from the 40 deg camera, so wall colour and columns compare two different walls.
